patch.value: A VCS with no ignore mechanism can stage and then overwrite another VCS's control directory

Found by driving pm vcs through the real host harness. 'pm vcs add' with no arguments staged every file the working-tree walk returned, which included .git/objects, .git/refs and node_modules - 70 MB, and more importantly the git repository's own state. The next 'pm vcs switch' then tried to materialize a tree over those paths and failed only because git writes its loose objects read-only, so EACCES stopped it. On a tree where those objects were writable, a switch would have rewritten git's object store with whatever the target commit happened to hold at those paths. The engine was correct in isolation; what was missing is that a working tree is not the same thing as the set of files in a directory. Needs an always-ignored set covering other version control systems and the package's own control directory, a .pmvcsignore for project-specific patterns, and materialization that refuses to remove or overwrite an ignored path even when a tree names one.

add with no arguments never stages a path under .git, .hg, .svn, node_modules or the control directory; a .pmvcsignore excludes further patterns; materializing a tree neither writes to nor removes an ignored path even if a commit names one; a test drives this through the host harness rather than the engine, since the engine in isolation looked correct

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Fixed with two layers. ALWAYS_IGNORED covers .git, .hg, .svn, .bzr, _darcs, CVS and node_modules and cannot be negated - a project that could re-include .git could reintroduce the exact failure. .pmvcsignore adds project patterns with gitignore-like semantics (comments, trailing-slash directories, basename-at-any-depth for a pattern with no slash, ! to re-include). Three call sites needed it, not one: the working-tree walk, so nothing ignored is ever staged or reported untracked; materialization, which now filters the TARGET tree as well, so a commit recorded before the rules existed still cannot overwrite an ignored path; and empty-directory pruning. Verified against the real situation - a git checkout with a populated .git/objects - including a deliberately hostile commit whose tree names .git/HEAD, which materializes to nothing. Staging an ignored path by name is refused rather than skipped: staging nothing while reporting success is how a commit ends up missing a file. Rules are read per call, not cached, because .pmvcsignore is itself tracked and a switch can change it.

patch.value: Implemented and verified: an always-ignored set plus .pmvcsignore, applied at the working-tree walk, at materialization and at explicit staging
